title: Mother Tongue Language Exemption for Special Educational Needs Students
what_it_is: Mother Tongue Language Exemption for Special Educational Needs Students

sections.label: PSLE MTL exemption questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about the new PSLE scoring system for Mother Tongue Language exemption for Special Educational Needs students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the new PSLE scoring system (a) what is the rationale of assigning the lowest three levels of the eight Achievement Levels in Mother Tongue Language (MTL) for Special Educational Needs (SEN) students who are granted exemptions; (b) what is the impact on PSLE results, course eligibility and school choices between the current and new scoring system for MTL exemption; (c) whether the Ministry will consider delaying the implementation of the MTL exemption scoring changes for the current cohorts who will be affected; and (d) whether the Ministry will consider an alternate PSLE aggregate scoring system for SEN students who are granted MTL exemption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will address the concerns of families and educators that Special Educational Needs (SEN) students deemed not suitable to take Mother Tongue Language (MTL) as an examinable subject, are being further disadvantaged at an early age; and (b) whether more inclusive mainstream secondary schools can be developed by modifying the Secondary 1 Direct School Admission system to allow more admissions of SEN students affected by the MTL exemption scoring changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether students granted exemption from studying mother tongue languages on medical grounds may be exempted from the new PSLE scoring system taking effect from 2021; (b) what is the number of currently enrolled primary school students who have been exempted from studying mother tongue languages and will now be subject to the new PSLE scoring system from 2021; and (c) what is the rationale for applying the new PSLE scoring system to these students who received exemptions from studying mother tongue languages under the prevailing system.

sections.label: MTL exemption average rate
sections.summary: On average, about 4.5% of students are exempted from MTL each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In any given year, on average, about 4.5% of our students are exempted from MTL.

sections.label: AL system MTL score range
sections.summary: Under the AL system, the assigned MTL score ranges from AL6 to AL8.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What is specific to the AL system is that the assigned MTL score will range from AL6 to AL8.

sections.label: Secondary 1 DSA admission proportion
sections.summary: Most schools can now admit 20% of Secondary 1 intake via DSA, up from 10% in 2017, and many have not reached this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Most schools can now admit 20% of their Secondary 1 intake via DSA, up from 10% in 2017, and many schools have yet to reach this proportion.

sections.label: PSLE scoring and posting comparability
sections.summary: A small group cannot remain under the T-score system as their scores would not be comparable for secondary school posting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Given that we are changing the national examination scoring system, it would not be feasible for a small group to remain under the T-score system or to use an aggregate score of three scores, as their scores would not be comparable with the aggregate scores of other students for purposes of secondary school posting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Ultimately, in grading, scores have to reflect standards, instead of effort or circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The changes to the PSLE scoring, expansion of DSA and journey to Full Subject-Based Banding (SBB) aim to shift our education system away from an over-emphasis on academic results and encourage our students to focus on their own learning.

sections.label: Medical exemption conditions question
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOE will consider a medical exemption as an exemption with no conditions attached.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, to ask the Minister that if the reason for exemption is valid, is medical, then will MOE consider an exemption as an exemption with no conditions attached?

sections.label: Mother Tongue exemption grandfathering request
sections.summary: A request asks MOE to delay the new system and grandfather current Primary 1 to Primary 4 cohorts, starting full exemption from 2020 Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can an exemption be an exemption with no conditions attached?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, for those who are currently already in the Primary 1 to Primary 4 cohorts, so-called in-flight, the families had not made informed decisions at the time when they appealed for Mother Tongue exemption or language studies exemption, whether under the old or the new system now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, would MOE please consider delaying the implementation for this group and grandfathering the current Primary 1s to Primary 4s, start the new system preferably full and not conditional exemption from the 2020 Primary 1 cohort onwards?

sections.label: New PSLE AL scoring system
sections.summary: The new PSLE AL scoring system will come into effect for the PSLE cohort in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The thing is this: the new PSLE AL scoring system will come into effect for the PSLE cohort in 2021.

sections.label: Foundation MTL score range
sections.summary: Scores are assigned by reference to peers, including Foundation MTL takers, whose scores largely fall within AL6 to AL8.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, to be fair, we have to assign a score, and we do that by taking reference from their peers, including those who take Foundation MTL.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, actually, the range of scores for those who take Foundation MTL, by and large, falls within AL6 to AL8.
